claims: For a cone with top radius R and height H, r=Rh/H, so V(h)=pi R² h³/(3H²). For fraction f of total volume, h/H=f^(1/3). Half height contains one eighth volume; half volume gives about 79.37 percent height.

A comparison cylinder of the same height has radius R/sqrt(3), giving equal total capacity. Constant inflow gives linear volume growth in both, while its depth is linear only in the cylinder. No outflow or changing vessel geometry during the pour.

checks.description: Cylinder and cone total volumes agree
Half volume is approximately four fifths height
Rate of rise decreases as cone fills

limitations: Numerical checks complement derivations. Idealized assumptions are stated; illustrative objects are not experimental data.
